# Power Platform Code Apps + Dataverse

This skill packages field-tested patterns for taking a Power Apps **Code App** (a React/Vite app generated by tools like vibe.powerapps.com, or built from scratch) from "in-memory mock data" to a real, production-ready Dataverse-backed solution — including schema provisioning, security, auditing, and solution packaging, all done directly against the Dataverse Web API rather than through the portal UI.

It contains no project-specific business content — only the mechanics of the platform.

## When to use this

- The user has a Code App (React/Vite, `power.config.json`, `src/generated/*`) they want to connect to real Dataverse tables instead of in-memory data.
- The user needs to create Dataverse tables/columns/relationships programmatically (faster and more repeatable than clicking through make.powerapps.com for dozens of columns).
- The user needs security roles, native Dataverse auditing, a model-driven app (sitemap/AppModule/forms) alongside — or entirely instead of — the Code App, or a clean exportable managed solution.
- The user wants a **pure, license-free model-driven app** on existing tables (no Code App at all) — full forms, related-record subgrids, and dashboards, all plain declarative FormXml, see [references/model-driven-app.md](references/model-driven-app.md), including which model-driven customizations stay license-free (plain forms/views/sitemaps/subgrids/dashboards) versus which typically require an additional Power Apps license (Custom Pages / embedded Canvas Apps, PCF controls calling external services, premium connectors, AI Builder/Copilot).
- **More than one app (Code App, Model-driven App, another Canvas App, an integration) reads/writes the same Dataverse tables** — see [references/multi-app-data-integrity.md](references/multi-app-data-integrity.md) for why "required field" constraints and async auto-fill flows aren't enough on their own to stop one app from crashing on data another app left incomplete, and what actually is.
- The user wants to wire a Code App to a **non-Dataverse connector** data source (Copilot Studio, SharePoint, or any other standard/premium connector) — e.g. calling an existing Copilot Studio agent for a similarity/lookup feature — see [references/connector-data-sources.md](references/connector-data-sources.md) for the connection-must-pre-exist requirement, the Git Bash path-mangling gotcha, and a client-side singleton bug that silently breaks connector calls even when everything server-side is correctly provisioned.
- The user hits a Code App deployment error (broken images, `power-apps push` failures, table deletion blocked, etc.), a security/permission error for a specific user, or an "it's required but got saved blank anyway" surprise — see [references/troubleshooting.md](references/troubleshooting.md).

## Prerequisites

- Azure CLI (`az`) logged in as a user with at least **System Customizer** (ideally **System Administrator**) on the target Dataverse environment: `az login`.
- Node.js for running Web API provisioning scripts and for the Code App's own build tooling.
- PAC CLI (`pac`) for user/role assignment and solution import/export convenience commands — optional, most things are also doable via raw Web API calls.
- The environment must have **"Enable code apps"** turned on (Power Platform Admin Center → Environments → select environment → Settings) before a Code App can be pushed to it.

## Workflow

1. **Design the schema** — table list, columns, relationships, dependency order (tables with no lookups first). See [references/dataverse-web-api.md](references/dataverse-web-api.md).
2. **Provision Dataverse** — publisher, solution, tables, columns, relationships via raw Web API calls (idempotent scripts, re-runnable). Same reference.
3. **Wire the Code App to Dataverse** — flip data-source config from in-memory to Dataverse, regenerate/adjust generated hooks/models. See [references/code-app-deployment.md](references/code-app-deployment.md). For a **non-Dataverse connector** data source instead (or in addition), see [references/connector-data-sources.md](references/connector-data-sources.md).
4. **Add security & governance** — real Dataverse security roles + native auditing instead of hand-rolled "governance tables". See [references/security-and-audit.md](references/security-and-audit.md).
5. **(Optional) Add a model-driven app** alongside — or entirely instead of — the Code App for admin/ops screens backed by the same tables: sitemap + AppModule, real main forms (FormXml) if the auto-generated 2-field default isn't enough, related-record subgrids, and native dashboards. A Dataverse component (table, role) can belong to more than one solution at once, so a second, standalone model-driven app can reuse an existing Code App project's tables/roles additively, without touching its solution. See [references/model-driven-app.md](references/model-driven-app.md).
6. **The moment a second app can write to the same tables, re-check every non-null assumption the first app makes** — required-field settings and client-side form validation only constrain the app they're configured on; a different app's rendering code needs its own null-guards regardless. See [references/multi-app-data-integrity.md](references/multi-app-data-integrity.md).
7. **Test with a genuinely non-privileged user, not just a System Administrator account** — a custom security role built by script only has the privileges you explicitly granted it; a sysadmin test account silently bypasses every gap. See [references/security-and-audit.md](references/security-and-audit.md).
8. **Build & deploy the Code App** — `npm run build` then `npx power-apps push`. Watch for the static-asset bundling gotcha in [references/code-app-deployment.md](references/code-app-deployment.md).
9. **Package for production** — make sure the Code App, tables, roles, and sitemap all belong to one named solution; export a managed solution and verify it's self-contained. See [references/solution-alm.md](references/solution-alm.md).
10. **Keep docs honest** — before trusting a design doc's data model, re-read the live schema and diagram it fresh; exports and diagrams go stale the moment anyone edits a table by hand. See [references/dataverse-web-api.md](references/dataverse-web-api.md) §8.

Each reference file is self-contained with working request/response shapes and copy-pasteable script snippets — read the one relevant to the task at hand rather than all of them up front.

## Core principle: script the Web API, don't click through the UI

Every mutation in this skill (tables, columns, relationships, roles, privileges, audit flags, sitemaps, AppModule components, solution membership) can be done with a plain HTTP call:

```
<environment-url>/api/data/v9.2/<EntitySet or bound action>
```

authenticated with a short-lived bearer token from:

```bash
az account get-access-token --resource "https://<org>.crm.dynamics.com" --query accessToken -o tsv
```

Never persist that token to disk — fetch it fresh at the start of each script run (or cache it in memory with a naive expiry check). This means your provisioning scripts contain **zero secrets** and are safe to commit to source control as-is.

Write scripts to be **idempotent**: check for existing entities/columns/roles by name before creating, so the same script can be re-run safely after a partial failure.
